cues: Heat it, and the water leaves in clear stages.
At a hundred degrees, four waters go, and the blue fades to pale blue.
At two hundred and thirty, the last one goes, leaving white anhydrous copper sulphate.
At seven hundred and twenty, it decomposes to black copper oxide and sulphur trioxide.
